assessment: Selection, insertion and customer placement are candidate bottlenecks; combined timing and overlapping widths do not identify their causes. Two artifact-mediated alternatives merit bounded screening, with no demonstrated success yet.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: reusable order-specific checking mats can perform part of the completeness check through one silhouette per required component and an exterior-color reference. Empty or mismatched positions expose selection errors before assembly.
openings.delta: Transfers component accounting from workers remembering a mixed order to a visible spatial inventory; retains workshop assembly.
openings.prediction: Compared with the order slip alone, mats reduce undetected missing/wrong components and checking time, especially when alternating layouts. If errors occur after checking, mats will not improve packed completeness.
openings.probe: Use at most three spare-board samples for reusable mats. Alternate matched orders between mat and current checking, timing selection, checking, insertion and packing separately; independently inspect packed contents. Stop if mat handling erases savings or cannot fit the budget and fixed delivery schedule.
assumptions: Existing templates identify every required component.
Setup fits 500 units and recurring additions stay within 0.40 per order.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: an order-matched flat kit with corresponding marks on partition ends and base slots can let customers perform initial insertion. The interface supplies placement information currently supplied by workshop assembly and the generic diagram.
openings.delta: Removes workshop insertion from fulfillment while replacing layout interpretation with direct matching; supplied parts remain dismantlable and rearrangeable.
openings.prediction: Workshop time falls only if insertion savings exceed kitting and marking costs; customer short-partition placement improves only if ambiguity, rather than insertion difficulty, dominates.
openings.probe: Use up to twelve remaining samples to screen marked kits with ten participants across ordered layouts, including short partitions. Record unaided arrangement, insertion retries, separate workshop times and material costs. Require unchanged capacity, footprint, selected counts/color and rearrangeability; screen within the fixed deadline before any adoption. Pilot targets remain at least 59/60 complete, median workshop time at most eight minutes and at least 54/60 unaided arrangements.
assumptions: Marks remain intelligible during later rearrangement.
Marking and flat-kit protection fit both cost limits.
